claim: Received a DKIM-signed email addressed only to an address at this domain, signed with the domain's own key. Proves you had (or have) an address there, without revealing which.

nullifier.derived_from: pedersen(scope, length, lowercased recipient address): one claim per address

changelog: First release (badge.zeroknowledger.com and the zkbadge CLI).

rules: The DKIM signature verifies over the signed headers.
Exactly one To header, holding exactly one address.
No Cc header, and the signature's h= tag lists cc (so the absence of Cc is signed).
The key is published under the recipient's own domain.
The proof is bound to a one-time code, so it can't be replayed on another link.
Bcc recipients can't be detected: use emails sent only to you.
